**This is a novel depicting a historical figure.**

---

- **人物（じんぶつ）** — noun, "figure, personage, character." Kango: 人 (person) + 物 (thing/entity). Refers to a person of note or a character in a story. For Chinese speakers: 人物 in Chinese usually means "character in a story" or "figure" — very close match. [JLPT N2]
- **歴史上（れきしじょう）の** — 歴史 (history) + 上 (on/in terms of) + の; "in history, historical." 上 here means "in the context of." [JLPT N3]
- **描（か）く** — 他動詞, transitive; "to depict, portray, paint, describe." Counterpart 自動詞: none directly, but 描かれる (passive). Collocates with 絵, 小説, 人物. [JLPT N2]
- **小説（しょうせつ）** — noun, "novel, fiction." Kango. [JLPT N3]
- **だ** — plain copula. [JLPT N5]

"I will give you our reply after consulting with my family/people at home."

---

- **うちの** — pronoun + の, "my (family, household, company)." Familiar reference to one's own group. Context-dependent. Wago. [JLPT N3]
- **者（もの）** — noun, "person, people (humble)." Wago. Here used humbly to refer to one's own family members. うちの者 = "my family / people at home." For Chinese speakers: 者 is not used this way in Chinese — it's a Japanese humble reference to in-group people. [JLPT N2]
- **相談（そうだん）して** — 相談する (kango suru-verb, 自動詞); "to consult, discuss." て-form indicating sequential action. [JLPT N3]
- **から** — particle, "after, from." [JLPT N5]
- **お返事（へんじ）致（いた）します** — お返事 (reply, polite) + する humble form (致す); "I will reply." 謙譲語 (humble). [JLPT N3/N2]

"Please each bring your own passport."

---

- **各自（かくじ）** — noun, "each person, individually, respective." Kango: 各 (each) + 自 (self). Emphasizes individual responsibility. Common collocations: 各自で, 各自の. For Chinese speakers: 各自 is a close match in Chinese. [JLPT N2]
- **で** — particle indicating manner/means; "individually, on one's own." [JLPT N5]
- **お持（も）ちください** — お + 持つ (他動詞, "to hold/bring") + ください; polite request form. [JLPT N4]
- **パスポート** — noun, "passport." Loanword. [JLPT N4]

**I was so nervous that I started feeling sick.**

---

- **緊張（きんちょう）しすぎて** — 緊張する (kango suru-verb, 自動詞) + すぎる (to be too much); "to be too tense/nervous." て-form showing cause. 緊 (tight) + 張 (stretch) — literal "to be stretched tight." [JLPT N2]
- **気分（きぶん）が悪（わる）くなった** — 気分 (feeling, mood) + が + 悪くなる (to become bad); idiomatic: "to feel nauseous, to feel sick." Wago reading of 気分. Note: 気分が良い/悪い refers to physical well-being or general mood. [JLPT N2/N3]
- **〜て** — te-form showing cause/reason. [JLPT N5]

**It's too dark to see well, but I can sense that someone is there.**

---

- **暗（くら）くて** — 暗い (い-adjective, "dark") te-form showing reason. [JLPT N5]
- **よく見（み）えない** — よく (well) + 見える (自動詞, "to be visible") negative; "cannot see well." 見える is 自動詞 (spontaneous visibility). Counterpart 他動詞: 見る（みる）"to look at." [JLPT N4]
- **が** — adversative conjunctive particle; "but, however." [JLPT N5]
- **人（ひと）のいる** — 人 + が + いる (existence of animate things) attributive form modifying 気配. [JLPT N5]
- **気配（けはい）** — noun, "sign, indication, presence, atmosphere." Wago. Refers to subtle sensory cues suggesting someone/something is present. Common collocation: 気配がする (to sense a presence). No direct Chinese equivalent — uniquely Japanese concept. [JLPT N2]
- **がする** — idiomatic; "to sense, to feel (a presence, sound, smell, etc.)." [JLPT N3]

**I find meaning/purpose in my current job.**

---

- **私（わたし）は** — "I." [JLPT N5]
- **今（いま）の仕事（しごと）に** — 今 (current) + の + 仕事 (job, work); に marks the target of feeling. [JLPT N5]
- **生きがい（いきがい）** — noun, "reason for living, sense of purpose, worth living for." Wago compound: 生き (living) + 甲斐 (worth/value). 甲斐 originally meant "worthwhile result, benefit." Common collocations: 生きがいを感じる, 生きがいを見つける, 生きがいにする. For Chinese speakers: no direct equivalent; closest concept might be 人生价值. [JLPT N2]
- **感（かん）じている** — 感じる (他動詞, "to feel, sense") progressive; here indicates ongoing state of feeling. [JLPT N3]

**It is bad manners to eat making noise.**

---

- **音（おと）を立（た）てて** — 音を立てる (他動詞 phrase); "to make a sound/noise." て-form showing manner. Literally "to stand up a sound." [JLPT N3]
- **食（た）べる** — 他動詞; "to eat." [JLPT N5]
- **のは** — nominalizer の + topic marker は; "the act of... is." [JLPT N5]
- **行儀（ぎょうぎ）が悪（わる）い** — 行儀 (manners, etiquette) + が悪い (to be bad); idiomatic: "to have bad manners." Wago. 行儀 is specifically about table manners and social behavior, not just general politeness (礼儀). For Chinese speakers: not a Chinese word; closest is 礼貌 but 行儀 is narrower. [JLPT N2]

**The queen has elegance/refinement in both her appearance and the way she speaks.**

---

- **女王（じょおう）** — noun, "queen." Kango. [JLPT N2]
- **は** — topic marker. [JLPT N5]
- **姿（すがた）にも** — 姿 (appearance, figure) + に (in) + も (also/even); "even in her appearance." [JLPT N3]
- **話（はな）し方（かた）にも** — 話す (to speak) + 方 (way of) + にも; "also in the way of speaking." 〜方 attaches to verb stem to mean "way of doing." [JLPT N4]
- **品（ひん）** — noun, "elegance, refinement, class, quality." Wago (single kanji). Not to be confused with 品（しな）"goods, products." 品がある = "to have class/refinement." 品がない = "to be vulgar/crude." [JLPT N2]
- **がある** — existence; "there is, has." [JLPT N5]

**My older sister's back view (figure from behind) looks just like our mother's.**

---

- **姉（あね）の** — "my older sister's." Wago (あね). Used for one's own sister when speaking to outsiders. [JLPT N5]
- **後（うしろ）姿（すがた）** — noun, "figure seen from behind, back view." Wago: 後ろ (back) + 姿 (appearance). Often used emotionally — seeing someone leave, or watching someone from behind. A common literary device in Japanese. [JLPT N2]
- **は** — topic marker. [JLPT N5]
- **母（はは）にそっくりだ** — 母 (my mother, humble) + に + そっくりだ (exactly like, identical to). そっくり is an adverb/な-adjective meaning "completely alike, a dead ringer for." Wago. [JLPT N2]

**Because she does dance, her posture is always good.**

---

- **彼女（かのじょ）は** — "she." [JLPT N5]
- **ダンスをやっているので** — ダンス (dance, loanword) + をやっている (is doing) + ので (because); "because she does dance." やる is more casual than する. [JLPT N4]
- **いつも** — adverb, "always." [JLPT N5]
- **姿勢（しせい）** — noun, "posture, attitude, stance." Kango: 姿 (figure) + 勢 (momentum/force). Refers to physical posture or figurative attitude/approach. Here physical. Common collocations: 姿勢がいい/悪い, 姿勢を正す. For Chinese speakers: 姿势 is a close match for the physical sense. [JLPT N2]
- **がいい** — が marks the subject of the descriptive clause; "is good." [JLPT N5]

**My dog looks strong at first glance, but is actually a coward (easily frightened).**

---

- **うちの犬（いぬ）は** — "my dog." うち = my household/family (wago). [JLPT N4]
- **見（み）かけ** — noun, "appearance (at first glance), outward look." Wago: 見る + 掛（か）け. 見かけは〜だ = "looks 〜 on the outside." Contrasts with 本当/実 "reality." Often used with contrast: 見かけは〜だが、実は... [JLPT N2]
- **は** — contrastive topic marker; sets up a contrast with the following clause. [JLPT N5]
- **強（つよ）そうだ** — 強い (い-adjective, "strong") + そうだ (looks/seems); "looks strong." 〜そうだ with adjective stem = appearance/conjecture. [JLPT N3]
- **が** — adversative conjunctive particle; "but." [JLPT N5]
- **実（じつ）は** — adverb, "actually, in fact, the truth is." Used to reveal something unexpected. Kango. [JLPT N3]
- **こわがり** — noun/な-adjective, "cowardly, easily frightened." Wago: 怖（こわ）がる (to be afraid, 自動詞) nominalized with 〜がり. 〜がり attaches to emotion adjectives to mean "person/thing that tends to feel 〜." [JLPT N2]

**I knew the reason for Tanaka-san's absence, but I pretended not to know.**

---

- **田中（たなか）さんの** — "Tanaka's." [JLPT N5]
- **欠席（けっせき）の理由（りゆう）を** — 欠席 (absence) + の + 理由 (reason); "reason for absence." Kango. [JLPT N3]
- **知（し）っていたが** — 知る (他動詞) past progressive; "knew (already)." が = adversative "but." [JLPT N4]
- **知（し）らないふりをした** — 知らない (negative) + ふりをする (to pretend); "pretended not to know." ふり (振る) = pretending, feigning. Wago. 〜ふりをする is the key pattern. Can be used with any plain-form verb/adjective: 〜ないふり, 〜ているふり, 〜なふり. [JLPT N2]

**Because the station was dirty, I complained to the station staff.**

---

- **駅（えき）が汚（きたな）いので** — 駅 (station) + が + 汚い (い-adjective, "dirty") + ので (because); "because the station is dirty." ので indicates an objective reason. [JLPT N4]
- **駅員（えきいん）に** — 駅員 (station staff) + に (target of action); "to the station staff." Kango. [JLPT N3]
- **苦情（くじょう）を言（い）った** — 苦情 (complaint, grievance) + を言う (to say/make); "made a complaint." Kango: 苦 (suffering/complaint) + 情 (feeling). Note: 苦情を言う is the standard collocation. For Chinese speakers: 苦情 exists in Chinese but usually means "bitter feelings" — different usage. [JLPT N2]

**I wasn't keen to go, so I used a cold as an excuse to skip the drinking party.**

---

- **気（き）が進（すす）まなかったので** — 気が進まない (idiom); "to not be keen on, to feel reluctant." Literally "one's spirit doesn't advance." Wago. ので = because. [JLPT N2]
- **かぜを口実（こうじつ）に（して）** — かぜ (cold) + を口実にする (to use as an excuse); "using a cold as an excuse." 口実: Kango: 口 (mouth) + 実 (reality/substance) = "pretext, excuse." For Chinese speakers: 口实 exists in Chinese with similar meaning. [JLPT N2]
- **飲（の）み会（かい）を欠席（けっせき）した** — 飲み会 (drinking party, wago+kango) + を欠席する (to be absent from, kango); "skipped/was absent from the drinking party." [JLPT N3]

"What was your motivation for applying to our company's job opening?"

---

- **当社（とうしゃ）の** — 当社 (our company) + の; humble/formal business term. Kango. [JLPT N2]
- **求人（きゅうじん）に応募（おうぼ）した** — 求人 (job opening/recruitment) + に + 応募した (applied). 応募する (kango suru-verb, 自動詞): 応 (respond) + 募 (recruit). [JLPT N2]
- **動機（どうき）** — noun, "motive, motivation, incentive." Kango: 動 (move) + 機 (trigger/opportunity). Common collocations: 動機は何か, 動機を聞く, 動機が純粋だ. For Chinese speakers: 动机 is a close match. [JLPT N2]
- **は何（なに）ですか** — "what is it?" [JLPT N5]

**Section Chief Tanaka often makes sarcastic remarks.**

---

- **田中課長（たなかかちょう）は** — 田中 + 課長 (section chief, kango); "Section Chief Tanaka." [JLPT N3]
- **よく** — adverb, "often, frequently." [JLPT N5]
- **皮肉（ひにく）** — noun, "sarcasm, irony, a cutting remark." Wago reading of the kanji (not kango). Originally a Buddhist term (skin + flesh = superficial). Semantic drift: in modern Japanese, refers to sarcastic or ironic remarks, especially indirect criticism. 皮肉を言う = "to make a sarcastic remark." 皮肉なことに = "ironically." For Chinese speakers: 皮肉 in Chinese means "sarcastic/caustic" (adjective) — similar but the noun usage is more prominent in Japanese. [JLPT N2]
- **を言（い）う** — 言う (他動詞); "to say." [JLPT N5]

**In one's youth, it is natural to think about the meaning/significance of life.**

---

- **青年時代（せいねんじだい）には** — 青年 (youth, young adulthood) + 時代 (era/period) + に (in) + は (topic); "in one's youth." Kango. [JLPT N2]
- **人生（じんせい）の** — 人生 (life) + の; Kango. [JLPT N3]
- **意義（いぎ）について** — 意義 (meaning, significance, value) + について (about, concerning). Kango: 意 (meaning) + 義 (righteousness/significance). 意義 differs from 意味（いみ）in that 意義 refers to deeper significance/value rather than simple meaning. For Chinese speakers: 意义 is a very close match. [JLPT N2]
- **考（かんが）えるものだ** — 考える (他動詞, "to think") + ものだ (it is natural/expected that); expresses a general truth or expectation about human nature. ものだ here indicates what is natural or typical. [JLPT N3]

**My principle is that once I've said something, I always see it through to the end.**

---

- **私（わたし）は** — "I." [JLPT N5]
- **一度（いちど）言ったことは** — 一度 (once) + 言った (said, past attributive) + こと (thing) + は; "things I have once said." [JLPT N4]
- **必（かなら）ず** — adverb, "always, without fail, certainly." [JLPT N4]
- **最後（さいご）まで** — 最後 (the end) + まで (until); "until the end." [JLPT N4]
- **貫（つらぬ）く** — 他動詞, transitive; "to see through, carry through, persist in, maintain." Often used with beliefs, principles, or determination. Collocations: 信念を貫く, 主張を貫く, 最後まで貫く. Wago. [JLPT N2]
- **主義（しゅぎ）だ** — 主義 (principle, doctrine, creed) + だ. Kango: 主 (main) + 義 (principle). Used for personal principles or political doctrines (共産主義, 資本主義). For Chinese speakers: 主义 is a close match. [JLPT N2]

**The mind/spirit and the body are connected.**

---

- **精神（せいしん）と** — 精神 (mind, spirit, mentality) + と (and). Kango: 精 (essence) + 神 (spirit). Broader than 心（こころ）; refers to mental/psychological/spiritual state as a concept. For Chinese speakers: 精神 is a very close match. [JLPT N2]
- **肉体（にくたい）は** — 肉体 (physical body, flesh) + は. Kango: 肉 (flesh) + 体 (body). More formal/clinical than 体（からだ）. [JLPT N2]
- **結びついている** — 結びつく (自動詞); "to be connected, linked, tied together." 結ぶ (他動詞, "to tie") + つく (attached, intransitive). Counterpart 他動詞: 結びつける. 〜ている indicates ongoing state. [JLPT N2]

**In Japan, the 1960s was an era of high economic growth.**

---

- **日本（にほん）では** — "in Japan." [JLPT N5]
- **1960年代（ねんだい）は** — 1960 + 年代 (decade, era) + は; "the 1960s." 年代 attaches to year numbers to mean "the 〜s decade." Kango. For Chinese speakers: 年代 in Chinese usually means "era, age" — similar but less precise about decades. [JLPT N2]
- **高度成長（こうどせいちょう）の** — 高度 (high degree) + 成長 (growth) + の; "of high economic growth." Kango compound. 高度経済成長 is a well-known historical term for Japan's post-war economic boom. [JLPT N2]
- **時代（じだい）だった** — 時代 (era, period) + だった (was). Wago reading. [JLPT N4]

**My family has three generations living together.**

---

- **我が家（わがや）は** — 我が家 (my home, my family) + は. Wago: 我が (my) + 家 (home). 我が is a slightly literary/formal possessive. [JLPT N2]
- **三世帯（さんせだい）が** — 三 (three) + 世代 (generation) + が; "three generations." 世代: Kango: 世 (generation) + 代 (era/age). [JLPT N2]
- **一緒（いっしょ）に** — adverb, "together." [JLPT N4]
- **住（す）んでいる** — 住む (自動詞, "to live in") progressive; indicates ongoing state of living. Counterpart 他動詞: 住まわせる. [JLPT N4]

**In anything, the foundation is important.**

---

- **何事（なにごと）も** — 何事 (anything, everything) + も (inclusive "all"); "in all things, anything." Wago. [JLPT N2]
- **基礎（きそ）** — noun, "foundation, basis, groundwork." Kango: 基 (foundation) + 礎 (cornerstone/base). Used for both concrete (building foundation) and abstract (knowledge base, skill foundation) contexts. Common collocations: 基礎を築く, 基礎が大切, 基礎を固める. For Chinese speakers: 基础 is a very close match. [JLPT N2]
- **が大切（たいせつ）だ** — が marks subject; 大切だ (is important). [JLPT N4]

**This river's water does not meet the water quality standards, so you had better not drink it.**

---

- **この川（かわ）の水（みず）は** — "this river's water." [JLPT N5]
- **水質基準（すいしつきじゅん）を** — 水質 (water quality) + 基準 (standard/criteria); "water quality standard." Kango compounds. [JLPT N2]
- **満（み）たしていないから** — 満たす (他動詞, "to satisfy, fulfill, meet") negative progressive + から (because); "does not meet (the standard)." Counterpart 自動詞: 満（み）ちる (to fill up, be satisfied). [JLPT N2]
- **飲（の）まない方がいい** — 飲まない (do not drink) + 方がいい (it would be better to); "you had better not drink." Advisory pattern. [JLPT N4]

**I exceeded the Olympic qualifying standard and will be able to compete.**

---

- **オリンピックの** — "of the Olympics." Loanword. [JLPT N4]
- **標準記録（ひょうじゅんきろく）を** — 標準 (standard) + 記録 (record); "standard/qualifying record." Kango. [JLPT N2]
- **上回（うわまわ）り** — 上回る (自動詞); "to exceed, surpass, go above." 上 (above) + 回る (go around). Counterpart 他動詞: none direct. て-form connects to result. [JLPT N2]
- **出場（しゅつじょう）できることになった** — 出場する (kango suru-verb, 自動詞; "to participate, enter a competition") potential form + ことになった (it has been decided that); "it has been decided that I can compete." [JLPT N2]

**This temple is said to be a typical example of Edo-period Buddhist architecture.**

---

- **この寺（てら）は** — "this temple." 寺 is wago reading. [JLPT N5]
- **江戸時代（えどじだい）の** — "of the Edo period." [JLPT N3]
- **仏教建築（ぶっきょうけんちく）の** — 仏教 (Buddhism) + 建築 (architecture); "Buddhist architecture." Kango. [JLPT N2]
- **典型（てんけい）だと言（い）われている** — 典型 (typical example, model, archetype) + だ + と言われている (is said to be). Kango: 典 (model/canon) + 型 (type/mold). 典型だ = "is a typical example of." Passive of 言う indicates general consensus. [JLPT N2]

**When I hear a dialect, I am reminded of my hometown.**

---

- **方言（ほうげん）を聞（き）くと** — 方言 (dialect) + を聞く (to hear) + と (when); "when I hear a dialect." 方言: Kango. For Chinese speakers: 方言 is a very close match (same meaning in Chinese). [JLPT N2]
- **ふるさとを思（おも）い出（だ）す** — ふるさと (hometown, native place) + を思い出す (to remember, recall). ふるさと is written in hiragana (wago); kanji 故郷 also exists but hiragana is more common in this emotional context. 思い出す is 他動詞. [JLPT N3]

**This plant is widely distributed across western Japan.**

---

- **この植物（しょくぶつ）は** — 植物 (plant) + は. Kango. [JLPT N3]
- **西日本（にしにほん）に** — 西日本 (western Japan) + に (location of existence/distribution). [JLPT N3]
- **広（ひろ）く** — 広い (い-adjective, "wide, broad") adverbial form; "widely, broadly." [JLPT N5]
- **分布（ぶんぷ）している** — 分布する (kango suru-verb, 自動詞); "to be distributed, to be found across an area." 分 (divide) + 布 (spread). Used for geographical/biological distribution. 〜ている indicates ongoing state. For Chinese speakers: 分布 is a close match. [JLPT N2]

**Asia is currently undergoing major development/growth.**

---

- **アジアは** — "Asia." Loanword. [JLPT N4]
- **現在（げんざい）** — adverb/noun, "currently, at present." Kango. [JLPT N3]
- **大（おお）きく** — 大きい (い-adjective, "big, large") adverbial form; "greatly, significantly." [JLPT N5]
- **発展（はってん）している** — 発展する (kango suru-verb, 自動詞); "to develop, grow, expand." 発 (emit/start) + 展 (unfold/expand). Used for countries, economies, technology, or personal growth. 〜ている indicates ongoing process. For Chinese speakers: 发展 is a close match. [JLPT N2]

**Since the Meiji Restoration took place in Japan in 1868, Western civilization has been flowing in.**

---

- **日本（にほん）は** — "Japan." [JLPT N5]
- **1868年（ねん）に** — "in the year 1868." [JLPT N5]
- **明治維新（めいじいしん）が行（おこな）われて** — 明治維新 (Meiji Restoration) + が行われる (passive of 行う, "to be carried out"); て-form connecting to the next clause. 行う is 他動詞. Counterpart 自動詞: none. [JLPT N3]
- **以来（いらい）** — noun/suffix, "since, ever since." Kango: 以 (from) + 来 (come). Attached to a past event, indicates "from that time until now." [JLPT N2]
- **西洋文明（せいようぶんめい）が** — 西洋 (the West) + 文明 (civilization); "Western civilization." Kango. [JLPT N2]
- **流入（りゅうにゅう）してきた** — 流入する (kango suru-verb, 自動詞); "to flow in, influx." 流 (flow) + 入 (enter). 〜てきた indicates a process that started in the past and continues to the present. [JLPT N2]

**The spread/adoption of mobile phones is remarkable.**

---

- **携帯電話（けいたいでんわ）の** — 携帯電話 (mobile phone, cell phone) + の. Kango: 携帯 (portable) + 電話 (telephone). [JLPT N4]
- **普及（ふきゅう）** — noun, "spread, popularization, widespread adoption." Kango: 普 (universal) + 及 (reach). 普及する is 自動詞 (spreads on its own). Notable: 普及 is the intransitive form; there is no direct transitive counterpart. Common collocations: 普及する, 普及率, 普及が進む. For Chinese speakers: 普及 is a close match. [JLPT N2]

**I have forgotten the plot of a novel I read a long time ago.**

---

- **昔（むかし）読（よ）んだ** — 昔 (long ago, old times) + 読んだ (read, past attributive); "that I read long ago." [JLPT N4]
- **小説（しょうせつ）の** — 小説 (novel) + の. [JLPT N3]
- **筋（すじ）を忘（わす）れてしまった** — 筋 (plot, storyline, logic) + を忘れてしまった (have forgotten). 筋: Wago. Refers to the storyline/plot of a narrative, or the logical thread of an argument. Also means "muscle fiber" (as in 肉の筋) or "line, stripe." Collocations: 筋が通る (logical/consistent), 筋を考える, 話の筋. For Chinese speakers: 筋 exists in Chinese (e.g., 筋道) but Japanese usage is broader. [JLPT N2]

**I want to buy a new car, but I cannot afford it (do not have the financial margin). / I allowed extra time and left home 30 minutes early, considering a time margin.**

---

- **車（くるま）を買（か）い替（か）えたいが** — 車を買い替えたい (want to replace the car, buy a new one) + が (but). 買い替える is 他動詞: 買う (buy) + 替える (replace). [JLPT N2]
- **その余裕（よゆう）はない** — その余裕 (that margin/room/leeway) + はない (there is not). 余裕: Kango: 余 (surplus) + 裕 (abundant). Refers to extra room — financial, temporal, mental, or physical. Collocations: 余裕がある/ない, 時間の余裕, 気持ちの余裕. For Chinese speakers: 余裕 is used differently from Chinese — in Japanese it is broader (time, money, mental space). [JLPT N2]
- **時間（じかん）の余裕（よゆう）を見（み）て** — 時間の余裕 (time margin) + を見て (considering, allowing for). [JLPT N2]
- **30分前（ぷんまえ）に家（いえ）を出（で）た** — 30分前 (30 minutes early) + に + 家を出た (left home). [JLPT N4]

"Shipping costs will be borne by our company." / The cost of highway construction will be shared equally between the national and local governments.

---

- **送料（そうりょう）は** — 送料 (shipping cost, postage) + は. Kango. [JLPT N2]
- **当社（とうしゃ）負担（ふたん）とします** — 当社 (our company) + 負担 (burden, cost borne by) + とします (will be). 負担: Kango: 負 (carry/bear) + 担 (carry on shoulder). Refers to the burden of costs, responsibility, or workload. Collocations: 負担する, 負担が大きい, 負担を減らす. For Chinese speakers: 负担 is a close match. [JLPT N2]
- **高速道路（こうそくどうろ）建設（けんせつ）の費用（ひよう）は** — 高速道路 (highway) + 建設 (construction) + の + 費用 (cost, expense). All kango. [JLPT N2]
- **国（くに）と地方（ちほう）が半分（はんぶん）ずつ** — 国 (nation/government) + と + 地方 (local government) + が + 半分ずつ (half each). [JLPT N3]
- **負担（ふたん）する** — 負担する (kango suru-verb, 他動詞); "to bear (a cost/burden)." [JLPT N2]

**This product comes with a one-year warranty.**

---

- **この商品（しょうひん）には** — この商品 (this product) + には (for, on). Kango: 商 (commerce) + 品 (product). [JLPT N3]
- **1年間（ねんかん）の** — 1年間 (one year period) + の. [JLPT N4]
- **保証（ほしょう）が付（つ）いている** — 保証 (guarantee, warranty, assurance) + が付いている (is attached, comes with). 保証: Kango: 保 (protect/guarantee) + 証 (proof/certificate). 付く is 自動詞 (to be attached). Counterpart 他動詞: 付ける. Used for product warranties, quality guarantees, or metaphorical assurances. For Chinese speakers: 保证 is a close match. [JLPT N2]

**I called to demand/urge the repayment of money I lent.**

---

- **貸（か）した金（かね）を返（かえ）すよう** — 貸した (lent) + 金 (money) + を返すよう (to repay). 貸す is 他動詞. Counterpart 自動詞: none, but 借りる (to borrow) is the reciprocal action. 〜よう = 〜ように (so that, to). [JLPT N4]
- **催促（さいそく）の電話（でんわ）をかけた** — 催促 (demand, request, urging) + の + 電話をかけた (made a phone call). 催促: Kango: 催 (urge) + 促 (urge/prompt). 催促する is 他動詞. Collocations: 催促する, 催促の電話, 催促状. For Chinese speakers: 催促 is a close match. [JLPT N2]

**For a nation / law / budget / treaty / contract / transaction / business deal ... to be established.**

---

- **国家（こっか）／法律（ほうりつ）／予算（よさん）／条約（じょうやく）／契約（けいやく）／取引（とりひき）／商談（しょうだん）…が** — List of subjects: nation, law, budget, treaty, contract, transaction, business negotiation. All kango. [JLPT N2]
- **成立（せいりつ）する** — 成立する (kango suru-verb, 自動詞); "to be established, be formed, come into effect." 成 (become) + 立 (stand). Used for agreements, laws, organizations, or conditions that come into existence through a formal process. Collocations: 成立する, 成立させる, 取引が成立する. For Chinese speakers: 成立 is a very close match. [JLPT N2]

**What Tanaka-san says and what he does are contradictory/inconsistent.**

---

- **田中（たなか）さんは** — "Tanaka-san." [JLPT N5]
- **言（い）っていることとしていることが** — 言っていること (what he says) + としていることが (and what he does); ている nominalized with こと. [JLPT N4]
- **矛盾（むじゅん）している** — 矛盾する (kango suru-verb, 自動詞); "to be contradictory, inconsistent." 矛 (spear) + 盾 (shield). From the Chinese story of a man who claimed to have a spear that could pierce any shield and a shield that could block any spear — a logical impossibility. Collocations: 矛盾している, 矛盾点, 矛盾に気づく. For Chinese speakers: 矛盾 is a very close match (same etymology and meaning). [JLPT N2]

**There are many people in the world who believe in the existence of UFOs.**

---

- **世界（せかい）には** — 世界 (world) + には (in). Kango: 世 (world) + 界 (boundary/realm). [JLPT N4]
- **UFOの存在（そんざい）を** — UFO + の + 存在 (existence) + を. 存在: Kango: 存 (exist) + 在 (be present). 存在する can be 自動詞 (to exist) or 他動詞 (to recognize/acknowledge existence). Here used as a noun. For Chinese speakers: 存在 is a very close match. [JLPT N2]
- **信（しん）じる人（ひと）が** — 信じる (他動詞, "to believe") attributive + 人 (person) + が; "people who believe." [JLPT N4]
- **多（おお）くいる** — 多く (many) + いる (exist, are); "there are many." [JLPT N5]
